clue.text: Period after holiday, showing result of getting smashed

indicators.note: after says the period comes behind the holiday in the answer

parts.note: a break is a short holiday or rest
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone returns from a holiday and finds things broken, or wakes after a night of heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' tempts as drunk after a holiday, but here it means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: damage or broken items are what results when things get smashed.

clue.text: Support on royal ship for composer

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the support above the ship

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment
HMS, His or Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes Royal Navy vessels

explanation.surface: A support is fitted on a royal vessel for a composer travelling aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Johannes, the German Romantic, is a famous composer.

clue.text: Adequate time for lunch overturned? I'm horrified!

indicators.note: overturned says the lunchtime hour is turned upside down, written bottom to top

parts.note: one o'clock is a traditional time for lunch
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone shocked that their lunch has been knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sufficient, just as much as is needed.

clue.text: Relish plan to eject son out of bed

indicators.note: to eject says the son is thrown out of the plan

parts.note: a sketch is a rough plan
up means risen, out of bed

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to turf their son out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tomato sauce is a type of relish, a condiment.

clue.text: One whose contribution to life lacks recognition?

definitions.text: One whose contribution to life lacks recognition?

parts.words: One whose contribution to life lacks recognition?
parts.note: a life here is a biography, and the hidden writer of someone's memoir goes uncredited

explanation.walkthrough: 'Life' seems to mean existence, but it is a written life story.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer who produces a book published under another's name gets no recognition for the work.

clue.text: Trade in copper — order placed by good man

indicators.note: placed by says the order sits next to the good man, following him

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
St, for saint, is the crossword good man
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A dealer in copper is honoured with an order bestowed by a worthy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: custom means a shop's trade or patronage from regular buyers.

clue.text: Dress down at college bar untidily — I would

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford

indicators.note: untidily says the letters of bar are jumbled out of place

parts.note: I'd contracts I would

explanation.surface: A student at a college bar dressed scruffily admits they would.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to dress someone down is to scold them, the same as to reproach.

clue.text: Note a sailing haunt banning new liqueur

parts.note: ti is a note in tonic sol-fa

indicators.note: banning says the new letter is kept out of the sailing haunt

parts.note: a marina is where yachtsmen gather

explanation.surface: A notice says a yachting spot bans a new drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a coffee-flavoured Jamaican spirit is a well-known brand of liqueur.

clue.text: Minute on street regarding line to see old musician

parts.note: re means regarding, about

explanation.surface: A brief note on street regulations lets someone visit an elderly performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval travelling singer or player was an entertainer of old times.

clue.text: A daughter gets choice in child-rearing arrangement

parts.note: an option is a choice

explanation.surface: A daughter is given a say in how she will be brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking another's child legally as one's own is an arrangement for raising that child.

clue.text: Get into bar tipsily with no end of uproar

indicators.note: tipsily means drunkenly unsteady, so the letters lurch into a new order
with no says a letter is taken away from the word bar
end of picks the final letter of uproar

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles drunkenly into a pub, without causing any noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes R ('end of uproar') from BAR, leaving BA; 'tipsily' rearranges INTO plus BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to get something is to acquire or come by it.

clue.text: Portrait of idiot with crack

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool
to have a crack is to have a shot, an attempt

explanation.surface: A painting of a fool with a fissure in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A police photograph of a face is a kind of portrait, often jokingly applied to any snap of the face.

clue.text: Brazen curse-word putting out small worker

indicators.note: putting out says a letter is thrown out of the curse-word

parts.note: blast is a mild oath
the ant is the crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone shamelessly swears while throwing a minor employee out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: blatant behaviour is done openly and shamelessly, just as brazen conduct is.

clue.text: Stint bursar arranged for set of experts

indicators.note: arranged says the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A college bursar's spell of duty is arranged for a panel of specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a group of advisers or specialists consulted for ideas.

clue.text: Surprisingly ranked rapid transport system

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly highly ranked fast transit network.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, this means leaving the car in an out-of-town car park and taking a bus into the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a scheme of edge-of-town car parks linked to buses is a type of transport system.

clue.text: Old fines reportedly stop car making delivery

parts.note: F stands for fine (as on pencils), so two of them give fines

indicators.note: reportedly says the stopping word is heard, not seen, so a word that sounds the same is written

parts.note: to brake is to stop a car

explanation.surface: Old penalties for stopping a car came through the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is a ball bowled in cricket: this one spins from the off side towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a ball bowled with off-spin is a kind of cricket delivery.

clue.text: Fundamentally instructed to be confined to one's room

definitions.meaning: taught the basics of a subject thoroughly
kept in as a punishment, typically of a teenager

explanation.definitionFit: Being well schooled in basics and being kept at home as punishment are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Supporting case, say

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
an instance is a case or example

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to state the case they are backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: say, as in 'say, a dog', introduces an example just like the phrase does.

clue.text: Recent arrival working to be accepted by a teen that's spoilt

indicators.note: to be accepted by says the working word goes inside the jumbled letters
spoilt says the letters of a teen are messed up

parts.note: on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A newcomer gets a job and is welcomed by a pampered teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's spoilt' scrambles A TEEN to NEATE, and ON goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby is the most recent arrival in the world.

clue.text: Solar phenomenon in east twice encircling docks

indicators.note: encircling says the two east letters go round the docks word
twice says the east letter is used two times

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, to clip

explanation.surface: A sun event is seen twice over the eastern harbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the moon blocking the sun's light is an astronomical event involving the sun.

clue.text: Win over duke is supported by half of fleet

indicators.note: supported by, in a down clue, puts the fleet part beneath
half of says only the front half of the fleet word is kept

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships

explanation.surface: A duke wins someone round with the backing of half the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to charm someone out of hostility is to win them over.

clue.text: One seeking haul from bank?

parts.note: the bank is a riverbank, and the haul is a catch of fish, not a robber's loot

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests a bank robber, but the bank is beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fishing from a riverbank hopes to land a good catch of fish.

clue.text: Biro duo misplaced in private room

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters have been put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: A couple of ballpoint pens have gone missing in someone's private room.
explanation.walkthrough: A Biro is a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a woman's small private sitting room or bedroom is known by this French word.

clue.text: Fortune rejected by family around English novelist

indicators.note: by says the family part comes beside the rejected fortune
rejected means the word for fortune is sent back, written backwards

parts.note: lot means fate, one's fortune

indicators.note: around says the family word wraps round the English letter

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A family turns down a fortune that came to an English writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the author of The Lord of the Rings is a famous English novelist.

clue.text: Send earrings in part to get valued

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sending someone jewellery as a way to win their affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked or valued, so it can stand for getting valued.

clue.text: Start trouble after beginning of business run illegally?

indicators.note: after says the trouble comes behind that first letter

parts.note: to jump is to start, as in shock

indicators.note: beginning of picks the first letter of business

parts.note: to ail is to trouble someone

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble at the start of a business that operates unlawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an accused person who flees rather than appear in court after release runs off illegally.

clue.text: Child longing to return for some offal

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: to return means the longing word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A child wishes to go back for some more of the organ meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the bean-shaped organ eaten as food is one kind of offal.

clue.text: Vessel covering river showing flag in the wind

indicators.note: covering says the vessel wraps round the river letter

parts.note: a steamer is a vessel, a ship

explanation.surface: A ship sails over a river, its flag fluttering in the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long narrow pennant or ribbon flying in the breeze is a streamer.
